title: Multi-stakeholder decision tiles — sprint draft
content:
Purpose:
Quick, role-targeted one-page "decision tiles" for fast seller handoffs during pilot scoping and procurement conversations. Designed for a 10–15 minute tactical briefing with a buyer team that includes Product, Platform/Infra, Procurement, and an Integration Engineer.

Why this format?
- Sellers often face multi-stakeholder panels where each stakeholder cares about a different SLO (latency vs cost vs compliance).
- Long decks get ignored. These tiles are modular: pick 2–3 for a meeting and customize the demo prompt snippets live.

Structure of each tile (1 page = 3–4 bullets + 30s demo cues):
- Who cares (persona signal)
- Core objection / risk (one line)
- Quick evidence (latency/cost numbers, footprint, SLA)
- Rapid responses (3 rehearsal lines)
- Live demo cue + slide cue (what to show in the console or graph)
- Escalation / next step (commitable ask)

Tile A — Procurement: "Unit Economics + Predictability"
Who cares: Procurement / Finance (CPO, Sourcing).
Core objection: "We need predictable spend and vendor T&Cs for multi-year contracts."
Quick evidence: "Hosted API cost model: per-token pricing + predictable bursts. Example: 50M tokens/month estimate -> $X/mo using our standard gpt-like open model profile (Q3 benchmark). Dedicated Reserved: 20% lower unit with commit."
Rapid responses:
  - "Start with hosted + usage caps, convert to Reserved when usage stabilizes."
  - "We provide monthly forecast exports and token-level attribution per route for reconciliation."
  - "Contract add-on: committed throughput windows and surge buckets with SLA credits."
Demo cue: open Console > Billing > Cost by route for a 30s show of token burn and per-route trend.
Escalation: ask procurement for a 3-month forecast spreadsheet; offer a pilot PO for a 90-day pilot with a capped spend clause.

Tile B — Platform / Infra: "Latency SLOs and Fallbacks"
Who cares: Platform engineers, SREs.
Core objection: "We can’t tolerate tail latency spikes during peak traffic."
Quick evidence: "Runtime supports GPU pooling, continuous batching; typical 95th p99 numbers for chat path are: 120ms (p95), 420ms (p99) for small-context queries on Dedicated pools (internal bench). Built-in routing can route to a lower-cost variant on overload to keep p99 bounded."
Rapid responses:
  - "We recommend a canary with a 5% traffic slice and 24/7 sampling for 2 weeks."
  - "Enable prefix/KV cache for repeated flows — reduces tail by ~40% in our runs."
  - "Fallback policy: route to a smaller quantized variant with defined quality delta; we can instrument automatic fallback thresholds."
Demo cue: show Console > Traces > Per-route p99 toggles and a simulated canary rollout dashboard.
Escalation: propose a 2-week Dedicated trial with canary policy preconfigured and SLO dashboard access.

Tile C — Integration Engineer: "Onboarding friction and SDKs"
Who cares: Integration engineers, full-stack devs.
Core objection: "Our team needs quick integration patterns and predictable debugging hooks."
Quick evidence: "SDKs (Python/Node/Go) include local request replay, streaming sample harness, and a function-calling example for structured outputs. Example integration: 30 lines to wire a streaming chat with function calls and diagnostics headers."
Rapid responses:
  - "Share a repo template (we have a starter app that wires auth, streaming, and a test harness)."
  - "Offer a 1-hour onboarding pair session with solutions engineering to walk the pilot flow."
  - "Provide a preconfigured Postman collection and sample logs for common errors (auth, rate-limit, token mismatch)."
Demo cue: show the starter repo README + run a local streaming demo (30–45s).
Escalation: get a dev to accept a 1-hour pairing slot; follow-up with a sandbox token and repo link.

Tile D — Product Manager: "Quality/regression risk"
Who cares: PMs, ML product owners.
Core objection: "Model regressions or hallucinations will cause product risk."
Quick evidence: "Redwood Optimize includes prompt-set linked evaluations and automated alerts on regression. Example: we ran a real-time evaluation harness on a pilot and detected a 6% drop in factual recall after a model swap; rollback was automated."
Rapid responses:
  - "We propose an eval set for your top-30 intents and an initial alert threshold at 5% quality delta."
  - "Canary traffic and riff-back testing will prevent silent regressions in production."
  - "We keep model snapshots and diffs for auditing and rollback."
Demo cue: show Optimize > Eval set dashboard and example alert email.
Escalation: Request PM sign-off on eval set and a measurement plan for 30 days.

Tile E — Security & Compliance: "Data residency and auditability"
Who cares: Security, Legal, Compliance teams.
Core objection: "We need KMS integration, audit logs, and VPC/private deployment options for regulated data."
Quick evidence: "Private deployment supports customer-managed VPC/NAT and KMS/HSM key wrapping. Console logs include per-request audit traces and immutable export for 90/365 day retention (configurable)."
Rapid responses:
  - "Offer architecture diagram showing Private control plane + optional on-prem inference nodes."
  - "Provide a SOC2 / ISO27001 summary and a list of available integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault)."
  - "Propose a short compliance workshop to map controls to their policy checklist."
Demo cue: show the private deployment topology slide and sample audit log export.
Escalation: request a security questionnaire and offer a 2-week architecture review with security PM.

Tile F — Business Stakeholder: "Time-to-value + executive narrative"
Who cares: Head of Product/VP Engineering/CEO.
Core objection: "How quickly will we ship value and measure ROI?"
Quick evidence: "Typical pilot timeline: 2-week integration + 2-week canary + 4-week ramp to 50% feature traffic. Measurable KPI examples: NPS uplift on assisted flows, 20–40% reduction in average handle time for support bots, or X% increase in lead qualification rate."
Rapid responses:
  - "Offer a tight 8-week pilot plan with explicit success metrics and a go/no-go at week 6."
  - "Provide one-pager ROI templates for Sales and Support use-cases."
Demo cue: quick demo of pilot timeline slide and KPI dashboard mock (30s).
Escalation: ask for the executive sponsor name and schedule a 20-minute alignment call to confirm KPIs.

Operational tips for sellers (quick reference):
- Always open with the stakeholder map: ask "who will sign the PO?" and "who owns the SLO?"
- Propose concrete committable next steps (pilot PO, sandbox token, security questionnaire) at the end of the meeting.
- Use the Console as trust artifact: a 1-minute live tour of billing, traces, and routing shows operational maturity faster than slides.
- When in doubt: default to a short Dedicated trial with a fallback to Hosted for burst capacity.

Templates included (below):
- 1-paragraph pilot ask for procurement
- 90-minute canary runbook checklist for SREs
- 1-hour onboarding agenda for integration pairing
- PM eval set kickoff email template

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need updated benchmark numbers from Applied ML (p95/p99 by model variant for both Hosted and Dedicated) — action: @Miguel to attach the bench CSV.
- Legal wants a short standard clause for pilot PoCs addressing data deletion and exportability — loop in @Claire.
- Draft a tiny slide pack (3 slides) that maps each tile to an exact demo flow; include as an option for fast decks.

Quick attachments to create next sprint:
- Pilot PO template (procurement-friendly language)
- Console screenshot pack (billing, traces, optimize)
